title: Geometric two-isomorphisms preserve the ordinary scalar balanced pairing
statement:
Let $C,D$ be sites small in the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I,J:\operatorname{Sh}(C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(D)$ be inverse-image functors of geometric morphisms, that is finite-limit-preserving left adjoints [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and fix a natural isomorphism $\theta:I\xrightarrow{\sim}J$. Let $a:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of discrete commutative rings, with constant ring sheaves $R_C,R_D$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I_R,J_R$ be the module lifts obtained by applying $I,J$ to addition and scalar multiplication and identifying the inverse images of $R_C$ with $R_D$ by their canonical constant-section identifications. Then $\theta$ induces $R_D$-linear natural isomorphisms $\theta^R:I_R\xrightarrow{\sim}J_R$. Under the canonical constant-ring identifications its components on $A_C,B_C$ are identities and commute with $a$.

Write $E_C=B_C\otimes_{A_C}-$ and $E_D=B_D\otimes_{A_D}-$ for sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $e_I:I_BE_C\xrightarrow{\sim}E_DI_A$ and $e_J:J_BE_C\xrightarrow{\sim}E_DJ_A$ be the canonical scalar/pullback isomorphisms normalized by scalar insertion and the generalized pure-tensor formula [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction]. For every $A_C$-module sheaf $N$, one has
$$e_{J,N}\circ\theta^B_{E_CN}=E_D(\theta^A_N)\circ e_{I,N}.$$
For the universal balanced pairing $q:B_C\times N\to B_C\otimes_{A_C}N$, the underlying equality before passage to its tensor quotient is
$$\theta_{B_C\otimes_{A_C}N}\circ I(q)=J(q)\circ(\theta_{B_C}\times\theta_N).$$
The induced map of the scalar-extended modules is $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes\theta_N(m)$ on generalized pure tensors, with their balancing relations. These assertions hold for the module sheafifications, not merely on global constant sections [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $I$ and $J$ are specified composites of geometric inverse images, the same equation holds with $e_I,e_J$ expanded as their iterated normalized scalar/pullback maps under the canonical ordinary module composition identifications. It also holds termwise and naturally for cochain complexes and chain maps [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].
